properties.title: The Moon Dies and Lives Again
properties.speaker: GUkxa N!a’an
properties.summary: This story describes the waning of the moon as a death, and its re-growth as the promise of eternally renewed life.
properties.theme: Death, rebirth, continuity of life, cyclical time
properties.moral: Death is temporary or cyclical; renewal follows loss.

properties.title: The Honey and the Flies
properties.speaker: Dahm Ti N!a’an
properties.summary: When the god G!ara was still on the earth, he wanted to imitate the cardinal woodpecker by chopping out honey from a hive high in a tree. But he did not have the whistling magic or the ability to fly possessed by the woodpecker, so he fell to the ground and his stomach burst. Flies came and sewed up his stomach, and G!ara thanked the flies.
properties.theme: Humility, limits of imitation, interdependence, communal help
properties.moral: One should not imitate abilities they do not possess; help comes through cooperation.

properties.title: A Woman First Found Fire
properties.speaker: FAsa N!a’an
properties.summary: The first person to find fire was a woman. She sat by the fire and fed her children cooked food, while her husband slept in the dark and ate raw food. After waiting a long time, the husband stole the fire and ran off, and since then fire has been known throughout the world. It was a woman who first found fire because 'a woman naturally is a great thing.'
properties.theme: Discovery, gender roles, sharing, distribution of resources
properties.moral: Sharing resources benefits the community; women are the foundation of societal discovery.

properties.title: The Elephant First Found Water
properties.speaker: FAsa N!a’an
properties.summary: The elephant was the one who first found water. He hid it from people and drank it alone. But the mud from the water stuck to his ankles and his wife, the Beautiful Aardvark Girl, asked the others how he could have found water. Her brothers tracked him, saw him drinking water, drank it all up, and filled the waterhole with their urine. When the elephant returned, he tried to drink but it refused. He tried to grab his wife, but the brothers stabbed him to death with spears. The brothers were swallows that come with the rain.
properties.theme: Anti-hoarding, justice, communal sharing, environmental resource
properties.moral: Hoarding vital resources leads to destruction; sharing and community cooperation are essential for survival.

properties.title: The Ostrich and the Tortoise
properties.speaker: N!ani F’Kun
properties.summary: Tortoise and Ostrich were arguing. Tortoise told Ostrich, 'If I cook myself, you’ll eat me.' Ostrich said he would never do that. But Tortoise fooled him into eating from a pot of cooked tortoise eggs. When he learned what he had done, Ostrich vomited, kicked the pot, and has had red, split shins ever since.
properties.theme: Deception, pride, broken interdiction, physical evolution
properties.moral: Arrogance and greed expose one to deception; actions have permanent physical consequences.

properties.title: Springhare Dances
properties.speaker: Dahm Ti N!a’an
properties.summary: Springhare was playing and dancing, making rhythmic sounds. God watched him and decided to fetch a dancing skin from his son !Xuma. He gave it to Springhare, who danced all day. When rain began to fall, God asked for the skin back. Springhare refused and kept dancing. The heavy rain destroyed the skin, and Springhare fled into a hole. God used a hook to pull him out and beat him with a digging stick, explaining why people hunt springhares with hooks today.
properties.theme: Disobedience, greed, consequences, origin of hunting practices
properties.moral: Refusing authority and selfishness lead to severe consequences; resources given must be respected.
